articles.title: MSMED Amendment Bill 2026 Passed to Strengthen MSME Framework
articles.summary: The Parliament passed the MSMED Amendment Bill 2026 to strengthen the Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector in India. Key changes include improved delayed payment mechanisms, enhanced Trade Receivables Discounting System (TReDS), reforms in Micro and Small Enterprise Facilitation Councils (MSEFCs), streamlined Udyam registration, and measures to ease doing business. The ruling clarifies land ownership rules and reinforces the legal status of common lands under municipal governance.

articles.title: July 2026: Rivers Crossing Highest Flood Levels
articles.summary: The Dikhow river crossed its highest flood level (HFL) at the upstream Bihubar site in July 2026, a first in 28 years. Downstream at Sivasagar, the river has frequently crossed HFL since August 2018. Both sites are long-established monitoring points, with previous HFL records set in June 1998. The repeated flooding highlights potential climate-related risks that could require policy interventions.
articles.raw_summary: The Dikhow river crossed its HFL at the upstream Bihubar site for the first time in 28 years. However, at the downstream Sivasagar site, the river has been crossing the HFL frequently by small margins since Aug. 2018. Both are long established monitoring sites, where the previous HFLs were recorded on June 24 and June 25, 1998, respectively.

articles.title: ETtech Explainer: Why Meta's Zuckerberg may have to publicly bend the knee in India
articles.summary: A parliamentary panel sought an apology from Mark Zuckerberg over the removal of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Facebook post, warning that Meta could lose its intermediary immunity if he refused. During a meeting with Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) officials on Wednesday, Meta's chief global affairs officer Joel Kaplan conveyed Zuckerberg’s apology, sources told ET.

articles.title: ETtech Explainer: Meta's stop-start strategy for its open source AI models
articles.summary: Meta has introduced Glimmer, a smaller AI model with 30 billion parameters designed for tasks that can run on personal devices like Macs or PCs. The model aims to meet demand for AI systems that operate locally rather than in the cloud. This development could influence India's approach to AI regulation and local computing infrastructure.
